_comment: The accepted-red baseline for scripts/analyzers/complexity.sh, enforced by
scripts/ci/complexity_baseline.sh. Read that script's header before editing
this file -- adding a row here is a decision, not a formality.
T-complexity-8 sets the threshold at 8 and every entry below is over it.
They are over it deliberately. Each one is a Gherkin step dispatcher: a
regex chain in which every arm is a one-line delegation to a handler. By
T-complexity-8's own rule -- 'a function over 8 is carrying logic that is
not the match; extract that, do not flatten the match' -- there is nothing
to extract. The only way to move these numbers is a (Regex, handler) table,
and because the handlers are async with differing arities, a uniform table
in Rust needs a boxed-future wrapper per step: roughly forty wrappers to
replace forty one-line branches, which is exactly the 'indirection that is
strictly worse to read' that T-complexity-8 refuses. The 2026-08-12 entry
in docs/decisions.md says it in bold: do not flatten these into a registry
to make the number go down.
The scores are exact, not ceilings. A dispatcher whose score moves in
either direction fails this gate until the number here is updated in the
same commit, so the movement lands in a diff a reviewer can see. That is
the property actually worth guarding, and it is the one this project has
already been burned by: the 2026-08-12 log entry said 'three violations
remain' while steps/mod.rs::dispatch had gone 5 -> 9 inside that very
slice. The total held at three only because another function dropped off.
The correction on 2026-08-13 named the shape -- 'which is exactly how a red
gate gets waived on the next read'.
